title: small AI experiments deserve a price check before they run
description: Why small AI experiments need exact pricing and a run ceiling before they start.
tldr: A quick AI test can quietly become an expensive batch job. Check the exact model, endpoint price, and run ceiling before it runs.

sections.h2: why can a quick AI test become expensive?
body: Small experiments can expand into batch jobs without making the cost obvious at the start.
That shift turns a quick test into an expensive run, especially when the pricing and execution limit were never checked.

sections.h2: what should i verify before running a small experiment?
body: Verify the exact model being used, the price for its endpoint, and the ceiling for the run.
Those three checks make the intended scope visible before the experiment starts.

sections.h2: why does a run ceiling matter?
body: A run ceiling keeps a small experiment bounded. Without one, a test can continue quietly and grow into a batch job with a much larger bill.
The price check belongs before execution, while the experiment is still small enough to control.

faqs.q: How do I prevent a quick AI test from becoming expensive?
faqs.a: Verify the exact model, endpoint price, and run ceiling before the test runs. These checks keep the experiment within its intended scope.

faqs.q: What should I check before running an AI experiment?
faqs.a: Check which exact model will run, what the endpoint costs, and how many runs are allowed. The source finding is that these details should be confirmed before execution.
